public_body: Southern Berkshire Regional School District School Committee
overall: Committee violated the OML by deliberating via the Chair's October 7 email and by improperly discussing the email's leak in October 23 executive session; no violation on the other two allegations. Ordered minutes amended and released.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Committee deliberated via email on October 7 through the Chair's email to all members about a lawsuit and media inquiry.
allegations.key_passage: Here, we find that the Chair engaged in impermissible deliberation outside of an open meeting when she sent an email to the entire Committee regarding the lawsuit filed against the Committee and others, a matter clearly within the Committee’s jurisdiction.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged a quorum deliberated about the first OML complaint right after the October 23 meeting was adjourned, outside a noticed meeting.
allegations.key_passage: After review of the October 23 executive session minutes, and discussion with the Complainant, we do not find that the Committee deliberated outside of a meeting on October 23.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Committee improperly met in executive session on October 24 with counsel to discuss how to respond to the first OML complaint.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the Committee did not violate the Law when it convened in executive session under Purpose 1 to discuss the Complainant’s Open Meeting Law complaint filed against the Committee and the Chair.

allegations.summary: The October 23 executive session included a discussion of how the October 7 email was leaked and the need for confidentiality, which fell outside any permitted executive session purpose.
allegations.key_passage: The discussion regarding how the October 7 email came to be posted to Facebook and the need to keep Committee communications confidential did not fall within any of the ten enumerated executive session purposes.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Within 60 days, amend the October 24 meeting minutes to specifically list the October 7 email as a document used at the meeting.
Release to the public the portion of the October 23 executive session minutes reflecting the improperly held discussion.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that similar violations in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
